nodes.label: Spec 0004. One real primary path (Status: Proposed, 2026-11-15): designs the first real path through POOL: one psql client connects with TLS, proves who it is with SCRAM, is mapped to its own PostgreSQL login, and reads and writes real data on the one node that the journal, the configuration and a fresh probe all name as the writer; when the client leaves its backend is closed

Spec 0004 summary: the slice builds four things for the first time: the wire code (two new crates, pool-protocol and pool-core), the journal file with its bootstrap command, the probe, and the command pool run; it adopts the first runtime, TLS and SQLite dependencies and with them the first native code; everything else waits (no backend reuse, no extended protocol, COPY or cancellation, no replica, no status read or drain, no administration interface)

User stories of spec 0004: psql with TLS and an own password gets the same answers as from PostgreSQL; POOL refuses to send any SQL when it cannot prove which node is the writer (R-19); clear, bounded refusals when a limit is reached (R-13); a lost connection is reported as lost, never retried and never reported as a rollback (R-10); the session, lease and pool key records and the wire state machine exist with tests for scopes 005 and 006

Requirements section of spec 0004: 28 acceptance criteria cited as 0004 AC-n, covering scope 004 only; 'the fixture' is the environment the integration check starts (one PostgreSQL 18 container, test certificates and test logins) and 'hermetic' means a test that needs no network and no container

0004 AC-1 workspace shape (0002 AC-6): cargo metadata lists exactly five workspace members, pool, pool-config, pool-control, pool-core and pool-protocol, with exactly the six dependency pairs of the Workspace section; pool-protocol has no dependency at all; Cargo.lock holds the five members and the 70 third party entries of the rationale; apps/pool-cli does not exist; no package has dev-dependencies or a build script; cargo build --workspace --locked no longer prints 'unused workspace dependency'

0004 AC-2 source guard: rule W3 reads the new file format; tokio, TcpStream, TcpListener and std::net are accepted in crates/pool-core and apps/pool and rejected in pool-config, pool-control and pool-protocol; std::thread, UdpSocket, UnixListener and UnixStream are rejected everywhere; Instant::now, SystemTime, std::fs and std::env are rejected under crates/pool-control/src; rusqlite is rejected there except in journal.rs; StoredAuthority, StoreProbe, classify_startup, plan_bootstrap and writer_admission are rejected in every .rs file outside crates/pool-control; each of the six groups has a case in scripts/prove-checks.sh

0004 AC-3 dependency policy and notices (SEC-13, R-17): scripts/check.sh deny passes on the product lockfile and on both fuzz lockfiles with the deny.toml of the spec, which adds five license exceptions by crate and no license to the general list; a NOTICE file at the root names SQLite and AWS-LC with versions and license terms; scripts/check.sh linux-build passes with the native code compiled by the C compiler of the pinned image and no other tool

0004 AC-4 proof script and lockfile check: case 17 of scripts/prove-checks.sh rejects a wrong status whatever status scope 004 has; a lockfile entry ends at the next line that starts with '[', and one new case adds a local package to Cargo.lock and expects rule W4; scripts/prove-checks.sh passes on a committed tree

0004 AC-5 new keys: every fixture of spec 0001 and spec 0003 keeps its result and output byte for byte, and one of them changes its text to stay so: invalid-unknown-key.toml of spec 0001 names its unknown table no_table in place of listener, a known table from this slice on; each valid-serving* fixture exits 0 with exactly the valid report of spec 0001; each invalid-serving-* fixture exits 1 with its listed finding; a file without [listener], [limits], [probe] and [[principal]] is still valid, and each key left out has the default of the Keys table

0004 AC-6 names: a name or a path that holds a control character from U+0000 to U+001F or U+007F to U+009F, or one of the listed direction and separator characters, gives config.invalid_value at its key; the text CANARY-9f2c7b1e in such a value appears in no output

0004 AC-7 number of findings: validate keeps the first 20000 findings in the order spec 0003 fixes and counts the rest; the report then ends with 'findings omitted: <n>' in the human format and carries "findings_omitted":<n> before findings in JSON; a report with 20000 findings or fewer is unchanged byte for byte (made input 3 of 0003 AC-15 still gives 17268 findings); for made input 5 the binary writes exactly 20000 finding lines and less than 4 MiB in each format, and the omitted count is six times the entries minus 20000

0004 AC-8 configuration that can serve: ValidatedConfig::serving() returns a view only when the file has everything pool run needs and ValidatedConfig::probing() only when it has everything pool bootstrap needs; each missing piece gives one finding config.incomplete at its listed key; pool check-config does not report these

0004 AC-9 protected paths (SEC-4, T-11): pool run, pool bootstrap and pool show-authority exit 3 with state.permissions when the state directory is not a directory with mode 0700 or a journal file in it is not a regular 0600 file owned by the directory owner; they exit 3 with secret.permissions when a secret file has any group or other permission bit, is not a regular file or has another owner; a second command on the same state directory exits 3 with state.locked and changes nothing

0004 AC-10 journal on disk (0003 AC-7, 0003 AC-8): after a successful pool bootstrap journal.sqlite3 has application_id 1347374924, user_version 1, WAL mode and exactly the four tables of spec 0003, with revision 1, start sequence 0, hold none and one approved topology per cluster; the journal reader returns Absent for no file and an empty file and Unreadable for each case spec 0003 lists; each pool run that finds Ready advances the start sequence by one before it listens; in every other state the content of journal.sqlite3 does not change

0004 AC-11 bootstrap and reading the authority ID (0001 SC-8): on the fixture, with no journal and no witness, pool bootstrap exits 0 and prints a new authority ID; a second pool bootstrap exits 1 with bootstrap.store_present; pool show-authority prints the same ID and the state unconfirmed, and ready after the ID is written into the configuration; with an unreachable node bootstrap exits 1 with bootstrap.evidence_missing and creates no journal file; no command prints a host, a login, a database name or a path

0004 AC-12 probe (SEC-5, T-03): the probe logs in as the monitor login of the cluster (no superuser, no replication attribute, member of no role) over TLS with the CA and server name of the node, runs the one probe query and reports the system identifier, the role and the timeline; no answer within probe.timeout_ms, a wrong certificate, a failed login or a row of another shape gives a Failed observation; the control loop keeps one sample per node and build_snapshot never treats a sample as later than now

0004 AC-13 no listener without ready authority: pool run with a journal state of Uninitialized, Unconfirmed, Missing, Unreadable, Mismatch or Held exits 1 with the one finding of that state (the reason names of spec 0003) and never binds the listener

0004 AC-14 writer check before any SQL (0001 SC-8, PRD-005 AC-1): a session reaches PostgreSQL only through a route the current topology snapshot marks open for its cluster, and POOL checks the snapshot again after the backend is ready and before it sends AuthenticationOk; a backend that does not report in_hot_standby as off is closed; a closed or stale snapshot gives the client 57P03 and no connection is opened; on the fixture a node with another system identifier gives admission.changed with evidence.writer_identity and a refused login; hermetic: a running session is ended on a positive conflict and not for evidence.writer_missing alone

0004 AC-15 TLS and startup (SEC-1, T-01): psql with sslmode=verify-full and the test CA connects; a startup packet without TLS is refused with 28000 and no authentication request; GSSENCRequest is answered with N; a request for protocol 3.2 is answered with NegotiateProtocolVersion for 3.0; protocol major 2 or 4, a replication parameter and an unlisted startup parameter are refused with their listed SQLSTATE; a CancelRequest is read and dropped; toward the node POOL sends no startup packet unless the node answered S, the chain leads to the configured CA and the name matches; a wrong CA or name gives the client 08006

0004 AC-16 frontend authentication (SEC-2, SEC-3, T-02, R-11): the frontend offers SCRAM-SHA-256 and nothing else; the right password for a configured principal passes; a wrong password and a user name that is no principal both get 28P01 after a full exchange with the same message sequence; the verifier that POOL holds cannot log in to PostgreSQL, and the fixture uses a different name and password for the principal and the backend login; an authentication message longer than 1024 bytes is refused

0004 AC-17 identity map on a real connection (0001 SC-3, PRD-001 AC-1): an authenticated principal that asks for a database with no identity entry gets 28000 and the PostgreSQL log shows no connection for it; the backend login, the backend database and the credential come from the identity entry alone, and current_user and current_database() show the backend login and backend database of the fixture

0004 AC-18 the walking result (PRD-001 AC-1): the same SQL file run through psql directly against PostgreSQL as the backend login and through POOL as the principal gives the same output byte for byte: the committed INSERT, the SELECT of it and a deliberate error with its SQLSTATE; through POOL pg_is_in_recovery() is false and the system identifier is the configured one

0004 AC-19 teardown (0001 SC-6): a client that disconnects after an INSERT inside an open transaction leaves no row: a fresh connection does not see it, the backend process is gone from pg_stat_activity, and with limits.session_max_count = 1 the next login succeeds, which shows the session permit came back; the same holds after a clean Terminate

0004 AC-20 limits (first case of PRD-001 AC-3, SEC-8): with small limits on the fixture, a Query larger than limits.frontend_message_max_bytes gets 54000 and no byte of it reaches PostgreSQL; an oversized startup packet is refused; one session more than limits.session_max_count gets 53300; one waiter more than limits.backend_wait_max_count gets 53300 at once; a waiter gets 53300 after limits.backend_acquire_timeout_ms and not more than 2 seconds after it; a silent client is closed after limits.startup_timeout_ms; after each case a normal login succeeds

0004 AC-21 memory budget (first case of PRD-001 AC-3, R-13): with 32 sessions that each asked for 256 MiB of rows and then stopped reading, the resident memory of the pool process stays below 96 MiB (64 MiB for the process and 1 MiB for each session); a single row of 64 MiB passes through unchanged

0004 AC-22 lost COMMIT response (first case of PRD-001 AC-4, 0001 SC-6, T-07, R-10): the connection between POOL and PostgreSQL is cut after PostgreSQL answered a COMMIT and before POOL received the answer; the client gets one error with SQLSTATE 08007 and its connection is closed; the PostgreSQL log shows that COMMIT exactly once and no new connection for that login; a fresh connection finds the row, so POOL made no claim of a rollback

0004 AC-23 protocol subset and session records (0001 SC-1, SC-2, SC-9): after ReadyForQuery POOL accepts Query and Terminate; every other frontend message, and a COPY response from the backend, ends the session with 0A000 and closes the backend; an unknown tag or a length below 4 ends it with 08P01; the BackendKeyData of PostgreSQL never reaches the client; each session has one lease with a new lease generation and a pool key with the eight parts of 0001 SC-2

0004 AC-24 log events and redaction (SEC-11, T-12): every line pool run writes to stderr after it started is one JSON object with ts, level and event first; over a whole run of the integration check no line of stdout or stderr holds a password, a verifier, the canary SQL text, a principal, a login, a database name, a host or a file path of the fixture; Debug of every secret type prints [REDACTED]

0004 AC-25 shutdown: on SIGTERM or SIGINT the daemon stops accepting, ends idle sessions with 57P01, ends the others when they become idle or when limits.shutdown_timeout_ms has passed, and exits 0; a session that is ended while a query is in flight gets 08007 and never 57P01

0004 AC-26 integration check: scripts/check.sh integration starts PostgreSQL from the image pinned by digest in that script, runs the tests of the integration check and removes every container it started, also after a failure; without a Docker daemon it exits 3; the tests read addresses from the environment the script sets and contact nothing else

0004 AC-27 fuzzing (R-12, T-01): crates/pool-protocol/fuzz/ holds the targets startup, frontend_message and scram; scripts/check.sh fuzz builds every target of both fuzz packages, runs each on its committed inputs for a bounded time and ends without a crash file

0004 AC-28 frames split at every byte (R-01): for each golden startup packet and each golden message, feeding the decoder the bytes in two pieces split at every position gives the same result as feeding them whole; no decoder allocates from a length field before it has checked it against the limit

Spec 0004 table of what each criterion answers: AC-15 to AC-19 the scope 004 sentence (one authenticated TLS client through POOL to one primary, write and read real data, close cleanly); AC-18, AC-20, AC-23 and AC-19 its done when; AC-14, AC-17, AC-18 and AC-19 every sentence of PRD-001 AC-1; AC-20 and AC-21 the first case of PRD-001 AC-3; AC-22 the first case of PRD-001 AC-4 on a dedicated backend; AC-10 to AC-14 the minimum durable writer check from 003; AC-17, AC-19, AC-20 and AC-26 that a successful query alone does not prove teardown or denial

Spec 0004 table from the steps of the walking fixture to criteria: the same fixture through direct PostgreSQL 18 and through POOL with the mapped login, verified TLS and one dedicated backend (AC-15, AC-17, AC-18); the committed INSERT and SELECT and a deliberate server SQLSTATE (AC-18); a disconnect during a second, uncommitted insert, the backend exit, the permit return and the absence of the row (AC-19); a bounded rejection and a later successful login (AC-20)

Spec 0004 table of inputs from another spec or plan and where each is answered: spec 0003 Follow-up 3, 4 (with points m1, m2, m3, n2, m6, m7, t6), 10, 11, 12 and 14; spec 0001 Follow-up 2 (frontend authentication) and Follow-up 10 (the permission check of SEC-4, tracing); the ten safety contracts of spec 0001 (SC-1, SC-2, SC-3, SC-6, SC-8 and SC-9 are cited, SC-4, SC-5, SC-7 and SC-10 are not touched); spec 0002 rules for later slices and Follow-up 6; row 004 of the dependencies plan

Spec 0004: SEC-14 independent review is met by the scope box 'Review it (fresh model)'; the slice changes protocol, authentication and authority code, so the review needs the Security engineer, Protocol engineer and Control engineer roles of the reviewer roster, each of which a fresh model may hold for code

Spec 0004 Decision, chosen option: build the whole thin path now, with the wire code in two new crates, the journal and probe wired through a topology snapshot, and no client driver anywhere; the decisions marked heavy in the rationale are public contracts, formats or parts of the security model

Spec 0004 decision point 1: pool-protocol (new) holds the bytes: startup packets, message headers, error and authentication messages and the SCRAM text messages; it has no dependency and does no input or output, so it can be fuzzed and tested at every byte boundary

Spec 0004 decision point 2: pool-core (new) holds the data plane: TLS on both sides, SCRAM as server and as client, the backend connection, the session, the lease, the limits and the relay; it is the only library that names the runtime and a socket

Spec 0004 decision point 3: pool-control gains the journal file (SQLite), the conflict latch after a start, the observation board and the topology snapshot; it still names no socket, no thread, no runtime, no clock and no file call
Spec 0004 decision point 4: apps/pool gains three commands (bootstrap, show-authority, run), the log writer and the control loop that probes, publishes snapshots and writes the latch
Spec 0004 decision point 5: the probe reuses the backend connection of pool-core; no PostgreSQL client library is adopted

Spec 0004 decision point 6: six direct dependencies are adopted: tokio, rustls, tokio-rustls, aws-lc-rs, rusqlite and tracing; a person decides the two licenses they bring before the first of them is merged (manual step M1)

What this slice builds and where it stops (spec 0004 table): TLS 1.2 and 1.3 after SSLRequest with no plain text; SCRAM-SHA-256 against a verifier file per principal; protocol 3.0; Query and Terminate; one new backend per session; the primary profile on the eligible primary; session, principal, handshake, waiter and node limits with three deadlines and two size limits; the journal file, bootstrap, the start sequence and the conflict latch; a probe of role, system identifier and timeline; log events on stderr; configuration read once at start; later scopes 005 to 010 own the rest
Not in the scope 004 build: apps/pool-cli, an administration listener, a metric, a parser for SQL, a second process, and any command that changes a journal after bootstrap

Value sourcing table of spec 0004: the claimed principal is user in the startup packet; cluster, backend login, backend database and credential come from the identity entry resolve_identity returns and nothing from the startup packet; nonces, the mock key and the authority ID are random bytes of the operating system through aws-lc-rs; the eligible primary comes from the route view filled from build_snapshot; fresh_until is the sample time of the approved writer plus probe.observation_expiry_ms; now and sample times come from one Instant taken at the start of the daemon; the fixture image is postgres:18.7-bookworm at a pinned index digest written once in scripts/check.sh

Security model of spec 0004: anyone who reaches the listener may start a TLS handshake, bounded by one handshake permit, one startup packet, a few HMAC calls and limits.startup_timeout_ms (SEC-8, T-01); only a client that proves the password behind the verifier of a configured principal logs in (SEC-2); a principal reaches exactly the databases of its identity entries as their backend logins (0001 SC-3, T-04); two separate proofs; TLS required on both legs with no fallback (SEC-1, T-03); secrets in owner only files, read once, in types that print [REDACTED] (SEC-4, SEC-11, T-12); a node receives SQL only while journal, configuration and a fresh probe agree (0001 SC-8, R-19); no administration on the network

What the spec 0004 security model does not defend: root on the proxy host, a superuser of PostgreSQL and a client that holds a valid password; a valid client can hold a session and a backend up to the limits; one address that opens connections and sends nothing can hold every handshake permit for limits.startup_timeout_ms at a time; there is no limit per address, and a firewall in front of the listener is the answer until scope 005

Positive consequences of spec 0004: no application SQL can reach a node unless the journal, the configuration and a fresh probe agree, by the order of the steps; the client sees the truth about its backend and an honest error when the outcome is unknown; every refusal has a number a client library understands; the byte level code is fuzzed and tested at every byte boundary; memory per session has a bound; one crypto library does TLS and SCRAM and no PostgreSQL client library sits in the product; the review findings m1, m2 and m3 of scope 003 are closed in code with criteria; the source guard still means something after sockets arrive

Neutral consequences of spec 0004: the key names, finding codes, command names, event names and fields, the SQLSTATE table and the format of the source guard file are contracts from now on; 0001 AC-1, 0001 AC-12, 0001 AC-13 and 0003 AC-13 describe earlier shapes of the workspace and 0004 AC-1 is the current statement; rule W3 of spec 0002 keeps its number and message and gets a new file format; the words principal, verifier, monitor login and route view enter the glossary
Tradeoff of spec 0004: the product now holds native code, AWS-LC and SQLite; a build needs a C compiler, a flaw in either library is a flaw in POOL, and two more licenses enter the tree
Tradeoff of spec 0004: the lockfile grows from 16 to 70 third party entries; most new ones are small or for other platforms, and each one is still a package to watch

Tradeoff of spec 0004: the path is narrow on purpose: psql works, and a driver that uses the extended protocol, COPY, protocol 3.2 features, channel binding or options is refused, clearly, until scope 006
Tradeoff of spec 0004: a client cannot cancel a running query through POOL until scope 006; pressing Ctrl C in psql does nothing to the server
Tradeoff of spec 0004: every login opens a new backend and every logout closes one; that is slow, and it is the thing scope 005 exists to fix
Tradeoff of spec 0004: a client that goes away during a long statement is noticed late, and a client that reads slowly holds its backend with no deadline

Tradeoff of spec 0004: a conflict latch cannot be cleared in this slice: a second primary that was seen once keeps its cluster closed until scope 009, or until the operator stops the daemon, removes the journal files and the witness and bootstraps again (the second way out of walk 2 of spec 0003)
Tradeoff of spec 0004: a daemon whose journal is not ready does not start at all; the operator sees that in the service manager and not through a client error
Tradeoff of spec 0004: pool show-authority cannot run beside the daemon
Tradeoff of spec 0004: the timeline of a node in recovery is the best that plain SQL gives, not the exact replay timeline; it errs toward closing
Tradeoff of spec 0004: backend passwords must be printable ASCII; a password with other characters is refused at start
Tradeoff of spec 0004: a session that runs is ended when its cluster shows a positive conflict; that is the safe side, and it cuts work that might have been fine

Tradeoff of spec 0004: configuration that was valid and holds a control or direction character in a name is now refused, and a report with more than 20000 findings is cut; both change contracts of earlier specs
Tradeoff of spec 0004: the log writer is first party code; it is small, and it is one more thing that can be wrong where a well used crate exists
Tradeoff of spec 0004: certificates are read once; a renewed certificate needs a restart until scope 009
Tradeoff of spec 0004: the checks grow from seven to nine, and two of them need more minutes than the others

CI definition and manual steps section of spec 0004: no session edits .github/ or writes to GitHub; the manual steps M1 to M4 are the user's, or the lead's with the user's permission for each one, each with owner: user; nothing in the slice needs a VM or a PostgreSQL outside the containers the integration check starts, and no value in the spec is one only the user knows

Spec 0004 manual step M1, license decision (owner: user, needed before Build plan step 3 is merged): the Release maintainer decides whether ISC and BSD-3-Clause may enter the dependency tree for aws-lc-rs 1.19.0, aws-lc-sys 0.47.0, rustls-webpki 0.103.17, untrusted 0.9.0 and subtle 2.6.1 only; a yes means the five exceptions in deny.toml and the NOTICE file; a no for AWS-LC means the runner up ring, which needs the same two licenses, so a no to ISC itself stops the TLS decision of spec 0001 and comes back to the user

Spec 0004 manual step M2, CI jobs and the branch rule file (owner: user, after Build plan step 12): add the jobs integration and fuzz to .github/workflows/ci.yml after the job docs (ubuntu-24.04-arm, timeout 30 minutes, pinned actions; fuzz caches target/tools and runs scripts/check.sh fuzz-tools, then fuzz) and the contexts integration and fuzz to required_status_checks in .github/rulesets/main.json, in one commit so that rule C2 holds; Build plan step 12 adds fuzz-tools to the names rule C3 allows

Spec 0004 manual step M3, push, pull request and the rule on the remote (owner: user): push the scope branch, open the pull request, and after the nine checks have run on it apply main.json to the ruleset on the remote, as the remote proof of spec 0002 did for the first seven; until then the two new jobs run and do not yet block a merge

Spec 0004 manual step M4, Docker (owner: user): scripts/check.sh integration, scripts/check.sh linux-build and scripts/prove-checks.sh --with-linux-build need a running Docker daemon, and starting it is the user's

Document corrections of spec 0004 (six items in files the spec does not own): the SQLSTATE row of the shared conventions in docs/engineering-standards.md and five members; crates/pool-protocol and crates/pool-core in docs/repository-structure.md; a section 'Adopted in scope 004' in the technology evaluation; rows in docs/index.md for verify.md and the new context files; the agent guides, CHANGELOG, README, testing strategy, feature matrix and risk register in the Document it box; dated notes in spec 0001 and spec 0002 by the lead, applied on 2026-11-15

Workspace section of spec 0004: five members; crates/pool-protocol depends on nothing, crates/pool-config takes serde and toml, crates/pool-control depends on pool-config and takes rusqlite, crates/pool-core depends on pool-config and pool-protocol and takes tokio, rustls, tokio-rustls, aws-lc-rs and tracing, apps/pool depends on pool-config, pool-control and pool-core; internal-dependencies.txt (rule W5) holds exactly six lines and pool-core and pool-control are never a pair; forbidden-paths.txt (rule W2) loses crates/pool-protocol and crates/pool-core and keeps apps/pool-cli

Why spec 0004 creates two crates now and not modules in the binary: the frame code has to be fuzzed in the fuzz/ directory of the crate it lives in (spec 0002, rules for later slices) and a crate with no dependency keeps that fuzz lockfile small; the session code needs the runtime, and its own crate lets the source guard keep the runtime out of everything else

Where each piece of code lives in spec 0004: startup packet, message header, error and authentication messages, SCRAM message text and base64 in pool-protocol; keys, findings, views and generations in pool-config; authority rules, journal, latch, board, snapshot, probe query and row reading in pool-control; secret types and file reading, TLS setup, SCRAM, backend connection, session, lease, pool key, limits, relay and listener loop in pool-core; argument parsing, commands, state directory checks and lock, log writer, control loop, mapping into the route view and signals in apps/pool

Adopted dependencies of spec 0004: six direct dependencies declared once under [workspace.dependencies] with exact versions and features and taken with workspace = true: tokio 1.54.1, rustls 0.23.46, tokio-rustls 0.26.6, aws-lc-rs 1.19.0, rusqlite 0.42.0 and tracing 0.1.44

Spec 0004 dependency tokio 1.54.1 (no default features; rt-multi-thread, net, io-util, io-std, time, sync, signal, macros): the runtime, sockets, timers, the snapshot channel, SIGTERM and the log queue; macros is taken for select!, which the relay and the control loop need

Spec 0004 dependency rustls 0.23.46 (no default features; std, tls12, aws_lc_rs): TLS as server and as client, certificate checks and PEM reading through rustls::pki_types; tokio-rustls 0.26.6 (no default features) gives TLS streams on the runtime

Spec 0004 dependency aws-lc-rs 1.19.0 (no default features; aws-lc-sys, prebuilt-nasm): SHA-256, HMAC and PBKDF2 for SCRAM, random bytes and comparison in constant time; the same package rustls uses, so there is one crypto library
Spec 0004 dependency rusqlite 0.42.0 (no default features; bundled): the journal; bundled compiles SQLite 3.54.1 from source, so the format does not depend on the host
Spec 0004 dependency tracing 0.1.44 (no default features; std): the log events

Not adopted by spec 0004, on purpose: tokio-postgres (the probe uses the wire code of the slice), tracing-subscriber (the log writer is 100 lines of first party code), bytes as a direct dependency, ring, base64, sha2, hmac, pbkdf2, rand, zeroize and secrecy as direct dependencies, clap, thiserror and anyhow

Spec 0004 lockfile: Cargo.lock gains 54 entries for 70 third party entries in all, resolved on 2026-11-15 with Cargo 1.100.0 in a scratch project; if Cargo resolves another set of names in the real workspace the developer stops and reports it to the lead and does not edit the baseline to fit

Spec 0004 exit 3 finding codes journal.failed (a write to the journal failed, on pool run and pool bootstrap) and listener.failed (the listener could not be bound, on pool run)

pool bootstrap (spec 0004), seven steps where the first failure ends the command: validate and take probing(); check the state directory and take the lock; read the journal with Journal::read and the monitor credential and CA file of every cluster and node; probe every node once, all at the same time, each within probe.timeout_ms, onto an ObservationBoard; call JournalRead::plan_bootstrap (a refusal writes nothing); make an authority ID from 16 random bytes, create the empty journal file and call Journal::create; print 'bootstrap complete', the authority_id, the cluster count and 'next: add control.authority_id to the configuration' (JSON result created)

pool show-authority (spec 0004): reads the file, takes the lock, reads the journal without writing, keeps JournalRead::authority_id and classifies the start; it contacts no node and exits 0 whenever it could produce the report; result is one of uninitialized, unconfirmed, missing, unreadable, mismatch, restore_pending and ready, with the authority_id of the journal that was read; it is the way to read the authority ID again that 0003 Follow-up 4 asks for, and it needs the lock, so it cannot run beside the daemon

pool run (spec 0004), ten steps: validate and take serving() with ConfigurationGeneration::FIRST; check the state directory and take the lock for the life of the process; read and classify the journal, where any state but Ready ends with the finding authority.<state>; read every protected file; open the journal with Journal::open_ready, which advances the start sequence (failure journal.failed); build the runtime; bind the listener (failure listener.failed); install the log writer; start the control loop with an empty observation board, publish a first route view in which every cluster is closed, accept connections and write daemon.started; on SIGTERM or SIGINT shut down and exit 0; until step 8 failures are findings, afterwards every stderr line is a log event
Spec 0004: the daemon classifies once, and a journal state other than Ready is refused at the start and not served with every login refused
nodes.rationale: A process that looks alive and admits nothing is harder to notice than one that did not start

nodes.label: State directory and protected files (spec 0004): control.state_directory must be a directory with mode exactly 0700; pool.lock, journal.sqlite3, journal.sqlite3-wal and journal.sqlite3-shm in it must be regular files with mode exactly 0600 owned by the service account; a secret file (a credential, a verifier, the private key of the listener) must be a regular file after links are followed with no group and no other permission bit, owned by the service account; a certificate chain or a CA file must be a regular file that can be read; the code lives in apps/pool (the directory and the lock) and pool-core (secret files); all checks are for Unix

The service account in spec 0004 is the owner of the state directory; every check compares owners with it, so no call asks the operating system who the process is; running as root is not supported and nothing detects it

The state directory lock of spec 0004: the file pool.lock, created with mode 0600 if absent and locked with File::try_lock of the standard library (an exclusive advisory lock); when another process holds it the command exits 3 with state.locked; the lock is released when the process ends and the file is never removed; it is the exclusive lock 0003 Follow-up 4 asks for, so two daemons cannot share one state directory

Read limits of protected files in spec 0004: 4096 bytes for a credential or a verifier, 65536 bytes for a private key and 1048576 bytes for a certificate chain or a CA file; a longer file is secret.invalid

Content of a credential file in spec 0004: the password of the backend login or the monitor login; one trailing line end is dropped, then 1 to 1024 bytes, each a printable ASCII character from U+0020 to U+007E; anything else is secret.invalid; passwords outside ASCII need the SASLprep rules, which this slice does not build

Content of a verifier file in spec 0004: one SCRAM verifier in the form PostgreSQL stores, SCRAM-SHA-256$<count>:<salt>$<stored key>:<server key>, with a count of 1 to 600000, a salt of 1 to 64 bytes and two keys of 32 bytes after base64 decoding; the operator gets it from PostgreSQL itself (a NOLOGIN role with the password, rolpassword read from pg_authid, the role dropped again); the verifier is not a password and cannot be used to log in to PostgreSQL (SEC-2)

Content of the TLS files in spec 0004: the private key file holds exactly one private key in PEM (PKCS 8, PKCS 1 or SEC 1); the certificate chain file holds one or more certificates in PEM, leaf first, and the key must belong to the leaf; a CA file holds at least one certificate in PEM, and the system trust store is never used

One fixture of spec 0001 changes its text in spec 0004 (added on 2026-11-15, from a finding of Build plan step 5): invalid-unknown-key.toml held the table [listener] with the key port as its example of a table that is not in the schema; its line 3 becomes [no_table], a name of the same eight bytes, so the file keeps its length and every position, its finding stays config.schema at line 3, column 2, and the output of pool check-config stays the same bytes in both formats; the same change goes into the two in memory cases of 0001 AC-7 in crates/pool-config/tests/validate.rs (ac7_a_syntax_error_wins_over_schema_and_meaning_findings and ac7_a_schema_error_wins_over_meaning_findings)
nodes.rationale: This slice makes [listener] a known table and port a known key in it, so the file would give three config.missing_key findings in place of its one config.schema; no_table is not a glossary term and rule 2 of the configuration rules builds every name from glossary terms, so it cannot become a table of POOL later

nodes.label: The journal on disk (spec 0004): the format, the schema, the settings on every open and the start and migration rules are in spec 0003; this section fixes what that spec left to scope 004: checkpoint limits, busy handling, the reader, times, the file mode, storage failure while running, and the interface of crates/pool-control/src/journal.rs, the only file that names rusqlite

Spec 0004 journal settings: PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint = 1000 and PRAGMA journal_size_limit = 4194304 on every open that writes; busy_timeout is 0, because the lock on the state directory means no second process, so a busy answer is an error; created_unix_ms and changed_unix_ms are passed in by the caller, are for display, and no rule reads them

The journal reader of spec 0004: it opens the file read only, runs no statement that writes and runs PRAGMA quick_check; it tells an absent file from one that cannot be opened by asking Path::try_exists first; a file that SQLite reports as an empty database (page_count 0) is Absent too, because it is what a bootstrap leaves behind when it stops between creating the file and writing it, and it must not block the next bootstrap

Journal file mode in spec 0004: the binary creates the empty file itself before it calls Journal::create, with create_new and mode 0o600 followed by set_permissions to 0o600, so that a strange umask cannot leave another mode; it creates pool.lock the same way; SQLite gives its side files the mode of the main file

Storage failure while running (spec 0004): the journal is read once at the start and afterwards only written to set a conflict latch; when that write fails the latch still holds in memory for the rest of the run, the event journal.write_failed is logged and the write is tried again in every later round of the control loop; running sessions go on and new sessions follow the snapshot; this settles the sentence spec 0003 left open

Journal interface of spec 0004 in crates/pool-control/src/journal.rs: Journal (private, one connection) with read, create, open_ready and set_conflict_latch; LatchReceipt (private, cluster() and authority_revision(), built only by Journal); JournalError (Open, Busy, Changed, Write, as_str journal.open, journal.busy, journal.changed, journal.write) that carries no text from SQLite; and JournalRead

JournalRead (spec 0004): the private value Journal::read returns; it wraps the StoreProbe of spec 0003 and shows none of it; classify(config) calls classify_startup and gives an AuthorityState; plan_bootstrap(config, board, now) calls the function of that name with the samples of the board, the expiry of the configuration and the later of now and the latest sample time; authority_id() is the ID of a journal that was read, also when the witness does not match, and None when no journal could be read

Journal::create(path, plan, authority_id, created_unix_ms) in spec 0004: fails with Open when the file is anything but an empty database; it writes the marks, the four tables and the rows in one transaction, with revision 1, start sequence 0, hold none and epoch 1 for each cluster of the plan

Journal::open_ready(path, authority) in spec 0004: starts a BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction, reads the authority ID, the revision and the start sequence again and fails with Changed when they are not the ones the Authority was classified from; it then applies migrations (none exist for version 1) and advances the start sequence, returning the Journal and the new StartSequence; at the largest value it fails with Write

Journal::set_conflict_latch(&mut self, cluster, changed_unix_ms) in spec 0004: sets conflict_latched to 1 for the cluster and advances the authority revision in one transaction, returning a LatchReceipt; when the latch is already set it changes nothing and returns a receipt with the current revision; at the largest revision it fails with Write and the latch stays in memory
AuthorityState::name() in spec 0004 returns uninitialized, unconfirmed, missing, unreadable, mismatch, restore_pending or ready; the commands build their output and their findings from it

The probe (spec 0004): one task per node in the control loop; it keeps one backend connection open as the monitor login of the cluster and asks one question every probe.period_ms; when the connection is lost the next round opens a new one; the connection, the TLS check and the login are done by pool-core, called by the control loop in apps/pool

The monitor login of spec 0004: a PostgreSQL role with LOGIN and nothing else (not a superuser, no REPLICATION, no CREATEROLE, no CREATEDB, no BYPASSRLS, member of no role) that needs the right to connect to monitor_database; every function of the probe query can be executed by any role in PostgreSQL 18, run on 2026-11-15 against PostgreSQL 18.6 as such a role (SEC-5)

The probe query of spec 0004, sent as one simple Query message that returns one row with three text columns: system_identifier from pg_control_system(), pg_is_in_recovery(), and the timeline: in recovery the greatest of the checkpoint timeline_id, min_recovery_end_timeline and received_tli of pg_stat_wal_receiver, otherwise the timeline taken from pg_walfile_name(pg_current_wal_insert_lsn()); the first column is parsed with SystemIdentifier::parse

Where the probe of spec 0004 gets the timeline: on a node that is not in recovery it is the timeline of the current write position, exact, and it changes at the moment of a promotion (the timeline a node writes on now, which 0003 Follow-up 4 asks for, not that of the last checkpoint); on a node in recovery it is the greatest timeline plain SQL shows, which can be one step behind or ahead of the replay timeline
nodes.rationale: Both directions are safe for the rules of spec 0003: a later timeline closes writes and no rule opens writes because of a timeline on a node in recovery; the exact replay timeline needs a replication connection and the REPLICATION attribute, which is too much for a monitor; scope 007 qualifies this on a real replica

nodes.label: When a probe sample of spec 0004 is Failed: a row with another number of columns, a null, text that does not parse, a timeline of 0, an error response, more than one row or more than 4096 bytes of answer; at the deadline probe.timeout_ms for the whole round the connection is closed and the outcome is Failed; the sample time is the monotonic clock of the daemon read when the row has arrived; a Failed outcome replaces the last good sample of that node, so a node that stops answering loses its evidence at once

The probe connection of spec 0004 sets application_name to pool-probe and counts against the node, not against limits.node_backend_max_count; the operator reserves one connection per node for it in max_connections of PostgreSQL

PROBE_QUERY and observation_from_row(node, sampled_at, row) in spec 0004: the query text and the reading of the row live in pool-control as a constant and a plain function, so they are tested without a database; row is None when the probe did not get exactly one row

Control loop and topology snapshot (spec 0004): the control loop is one task in apps/pool that owns the Controller of pool-control, receives samples from the probe tasks over a bounded channel and publishes a route view to the data plane through a tokio::sync::watch channel; it runs a round after each sample it receives and at least once per probe.period_ms; pool-core never sees a type of pool-control

ObservationBoard (spec 0004, pool-control): private, at most one sample per node, with new(), record(observation) and observations(); record keeps the sample with the later sample time for a node and the one it has when the times are equal, so the list never holds two samples of one node (the first duty of point m3)

TopologySnapshot, ClusterAdmission and SnapshotGeneration (spec 0004, pool-control): a snapshot has a generation (the shape of TopologyEpoch, FIRST is 1) and one ClusterAdmission per cluster with cluster(), admission() (the WriterAdmission) and fresh_until(), which for an Open answer is the sample time of the approved writer plus the expiry and for a Closed answer is None

build_snapshot(config, state, board, now, generation) -> TopologySnapshot (spec 0004): calls writer_admission once for every cluster of the configuration with the expiry from config.probe(); it uses the later of now and the latest sample time on the board as its now, which can close and never open (the second duty of point m3); it is the only code that calls writer_admission in the product and the source guard keeps it so; the rule Fresh of spec 0003 is not made stricter

Controller (spec 0004, pool-control): private state, board, generation and the latches the journal does not hold yet, with new(state), record(observation), round(config, now), unrecorded_latches() and latch_recorded(receipt)

Controller::round in spec 0004 works in memory only and never waits for the disk: it builds a snapshot, sets the latch in the state with AuthorityState::latch_conflict (0003 AC-17) for each cluster whose answer is closed with latches_conflict(), puts the cluster on the list of unrecorded latches and builds the snapshot again, so the result already shows authority.conflict_latched; each round advances the snapshot generation by one, and when it cannot advance the round returns every cluster closed

Closing comes first, the disk second (spec 0004): the loop publishes the result of a round at once and only then calls Journal::set_conflict_latch for each unrecorded latch inside spawn_blocking, handing each receipt to latch_recorded; a write that fails leaves the cluster on the list, is logged as journal.write_failed and is tried again after the next round; so a second primary closes the cluster for new sessions as fast as a round runs, whatever the disk does

Cost of admission in spec 0004 (point m6 of 0003 Follow-up 4): a session reads the route view, one lookup by cluster, and never calls writer_admission; the function runs once per cluster per round; a bound for very large files stays open and scope 008 owns it, as spec 0003 allows

The monotonic clock in spec 0004: the loop reads it with one Instant taken at the start of the daemon and converts with MonotonicTime::from_origin; the data plane compares fresh_until with the same origin

When a running session is ended (spec 0004, a question spec 0003 left to this slice): silence does not end a session and a positive conflict does; the route view carries one flag per closed cluster that says which of the two it is, and scope 008 extends this with drain

Silence does not end a session (spec 0004): when the cluster closes with evidence.writer_missing alone (the probe stopped answering or its sample expired) running sessions go on and new sessions are refused; a probe that stumbles must not cut work that still flows

A positive conflict ends running sessions (spec 0004): when the reasons of the cluster hold evidence.writer_identity, evidence.writer_in_recovery, evidence.writer_timeline, evidence.second_primary, evidence.timeline_ahead or authority.conflict_latched, every running session of that cluster is ended: the backend is closed and at a message boundary the client gets 08007 when a query is in flight and 57P01 when none is; the node is then no longer the verified primary and POOL keeps writes on the verified primary only

The wire subset (spec 0004): what the protocol owner pins before code; everything in it is tested hermetically in pool-protocol and pool-core, and the parts a real client can reach are tested on the fixture

Startup (spec 0004): POOL reads the first 8 bytes of a new connection (a length and a code) with exact reads and no buffer in between; SSLRequest (80877103) is answered S before TLS and is 08P01 after TLS; GSSENCRequest (80877104) is answered N, allowed once before TLS; CancelRequest (80877102) is read, does nothing and closes with no answer; a StartupMessage of major version 3 is 28000 in plain text before TLS and is read and checked after TLS; any other major version is 0A000 and anything else 08P01

Startup packet rules of spec 0004: a length below 8 is 08P01 and a length above limits.startup_packet_max_bytes is 54000, both close the connection and the body is never read; a connection may send at most three first packets (an optional GSSENCRequest, then SSLRequest, then over TLS a StartupMessage or a CancelRequest) and any other order is 08P01; the TLS server offers TLS 1.3 and 1.2 with the defaults of rustls, asks for no client certificate and offers no ALPN protocol; direct TLS is not supported

Startup parameters in spec 0004: the body is pairs of text ended by zero bytes; a name that appears twice, an empty name or bytes after the end are 08P01; user is required and is the claimed principal, verified by authentication and never sent to PostgreSQL; database defaults to the value of user, is the requested database of the identity map and is never sent to PostgreSQL; application_name and client_encoding are sent to PostgreSQL unchanged; a name that starts with _pq_. is not supported and is named in NegotiateProtocolVersion; replication, options and every other name are 0A000

Protocol version in spec 0004: POOL speaks 3.0; for a request with a minor version above 0 or with a _pq_. parameter it sends NegotiateProtocolVersion with minor version 0 and the names of those parameters, directly after it read the startup packet and before the authentication request, and goes on with 3.0

The startup profile of spec 0004 has one value, DedicatedV1: the backend is opened with the mapped login, the mapped database and the forwarded parameters application_name and client_encoding when the client sent them; it is one part of the pool key

How each method names the principal (spec 0004): the slice has one frontend method; with SCRAM-SHA-256 the verified principal is the value of user in the startup packet, byte for byte, once the SCRAM proof against the verifier of the principal entry with that name has passed; the user name inside the SCRAM message is ignored, as PostgreSQL ignores it; the identity map is then asked with that name and the requested database; a slice that adds a method writes its own row here

Messages after login (spec 0004): after ReadyForQuery every message has a tag and a length that counts itself; POOL reads the 5 bytes of the header, checks them and copies the body through a buffer of fixed size, never holding a whole message

Frontend messages after login in spec 0004, read only while no query is in flight: Query (Q) above limits.frontend_message_max_bytes is 54000 and no byte is sent on, otherwise it is sent to the backend and a query is in flight; Terminate (X) is sent to the backend and both connections are closed; P, B, D, E, C, H, S, F, d, c and f (extended protocol, function call, COPY data) are 0A000 and the backend is closed; any other tag or a length below 4 is 08P01 and the backend is closed

Backend messages after login in spec 0004: T, D, C, I, E, N, S and A (row description, data row, command complete, empty query, error, notice, parameter status, notification) are sent to the client unchanged; ReadyForQuery (Z, length 5) is sent to the client, the status byte is kept and no query is in flight; a COPY response (G, H, W) is not sent, the client gets 0A000 and the backend is closed; any other tag, a length below 4 or a Z of another length closes the backend and ends the session as backend loss

Message boundary rule of spec 0004: a session is at a message boundary when no message from the backend is partly written to the client; POOL sends an error of its own only at a message boundary and otherwise closes the connection without one

Spec 0004: while a query is in flight POOL does not read from the client, so a second Query the client already sent waits in the socket; the price is that a client that goes away during a long statement is noticed when the statement produces output or ends; the transaction status of the last ReadyForQuery (I, T or E) is kept in the session for the log and for shutdown

BackendKeyData in spec 0004: the real one is read during the backend startup, kept in the lease and never sent; POOL sends no BackendKeyData of its own in this slice, so a client cannot cancel a query through POOL until scope 006 builds virtual cancellation credentials (0001 SC-9)

SQLSTATEs that POOL generates (spec 0004, the shared convention the engineering standards left to this slice): every error is FATAL and is followed by closing the connection, with the fields S and V (FATAL), C (the SQLSTATE) and M (constant English text that never holds a name, an address, a varying number or text from PostgreSQL); an error PostgreSQL sent during a query is passed on with every field; an error PostgreSQL sent while POOL was opening the backend is never passed on, because it may name the backend login; later slices add rows and do not choose again
Spec 0004 SQLSTATE 28000: a startup packet without TLS ('TLS is required') and an authenticated principal with no identity entry for the database ('no identity entry for this user and database')
Spec 0004 SQLSTATE 0A000: a protocol version, parameter, message or COPY that this build does not support ('this protocol feature is not supported')
Spec 0004 SQLSTATE 08P01: a packet or message that breaks the protocol ('protocol violation')
Spec 0004 SQLSTATE 54000: a startup packet or a message above its configured size ('a message is larger than the configured limit')
Spec 0004 SQLSTATE 28P01: a wrong password, or a user name that is no principal ('authentication failed')
Spec 0004 SQLSTATE 53300: no session permit, no principal permit, no room among the waiters, or the wait for a backend ran out ('too many connections')
Spec 0004 SQLSTATE 57P03: the writer of the cluster is not admitted ('the database is not accepting connections through this proxy')

Spec 0004 SQLSTATE 08006: the backend could not be opened: no connection, TLS failed, the login failed, the node is not a primary or the deadline passed while connecting ('the backend connection could not be established'); also the backend was lost while no query was in flight ('the backend connection was lost')
Spec 0004 SQLSTATE 08007: the backend was lost, or POOL ended the session, while a query was in flight ('the connection was ended; the outcome of the statement in flight is unknown')
Spec 0004 SQLSTATE 57P01: shutdown, or the cluster closed with a positive conflict, while no query was in flight ('the session was ended by the proxy')

Frontend authentication (spec 0004), six steps after a valid startup packet over TLS: POOL sends AuthenticationSASL with the one mechanism SCRAM-SHA-256 and never offers SCRAM-SHA-256-PLUS (SEC-3); the client's SASLInitialResponse must start with n,, or y,, and a request for channel binding, an authorization identity or an extension is 08P01; POOL sends AuthenticationSASLContinue with the combined nonce (its own is 18 random bytes in base64), the salt and the count of the verifier; the final message must repeat the header and the whole nonce with a 32 byte proof; POOL compares the SHA-256 of the client key with the stored key in constant time and sends AuthenticationSASLFinal with the server signature; no match is 28P01; each authentication message is at most 1024 bytes and the whole exchange has the deadline limits.startup_timeout_ms

A user name that is no principal (spec 0004) goes through the same six steps with a made up verifier: the salt is the first 16 bytes of an HMAC of the name under a key of 32 random bytes made at start, and the count is the count of the verifier of the first principal in the file; step 5 always fails, so a client cannot tell an unknown name from a wrong password, and asking twice gives the same salt

Spec 0004: AuthenticationOk is not sent after the SCRAM exchange; it follows only when a backend is ready, so a client never sees a successful login without a backend behind it; POOL as a server does no PBKDF2 work, because the verifier already holds the keys

Backend connection (spec 0004): pool-core opens every connection to a node the same way, for a session and for the probe: connect by TCP to host and port (a name is resolved by the runtime at each attempt); send SSLRequest and read one byte, anything but S ends the attempt with no fallback to plain text (SEC-1); run the TLS handshake with the certificates of node[].tls_ca_file as the only roots and node[].tls_server_name as the checked name (the TLS policy VerifyFull, a part of the pool key); send a StartupMessage for protocol 3.0; authenticate with SCRAM-SHA-256; read until ReadyForQuery with status I, keeping at most 64 parameter status messages (16384 bytes) and the BackendKeyData privately

SCRAM toward a node in spec 0004: the node must ask for SASL and offer SCRAM-SHA-256, which POOL chooses also when SCRAM-SHA-256-PLUS is offered beside it; its first message is n,,n=,r=<nonce> (the header n says POOL does no channel binding, the header y would make PostgreSQL refuse the login as a downgrade), the final message carries c=biws, the count must be 1 to 600000 and a wrong server signature ends the attempt; a node that asks for a clear text password, MD5, any other method or nothing at all ends the attempt

Spec 0004: the salted password is derived with PBKDF2 inside spawn_blocking and the two keys that come out are kept in memory for the credential, with the salt and the count they were made for, in a type that prints [REDACTED]; a later login with the same salt and count uses them again, so it is one derivation per credential and run and a burst of logins cannot keep the probe from a blocking thread

Spec 0004 backend connection step 7, for a session only: the parameter in_hot_standby must have been reported as off; a node in recovery reports on and an old or foreign server reports nothing, and both end the attempt; it is a check on the very connection the client will use, on top of the snapshot

Spec 0004: one backend attempt per session, with no second try and no other node to try (0001 SC-6); for the probe pool-core offers one more call on an open connection that sends one constant query and returns the text columns of its one row, or nothing

Session lifecycle of spec 0004, one task per frontend, the order of steps is the contract: 1 accept and take a handshake permit; 2 startup, TLS and authentication within limits.startup_timeout_ms; 3 take a session permit, then a permit of the principal (53300); 4 ask the identity map (28000); 5 read the route view, which must be open and fresh (57P03); 6 compute the pool key; 7 take a backend permit of the node or wait (53300); 8 open the backend (08006); 9 read the route view again and compare node, topology epoch, authority revision, the pool key and the configuration generation (57P03); 10 create the lease and send AuthenticationOk, the parameter status messages and ReadyForQuery; 11 relay; 12 close the backend, give every permit back and write session.ended

Spec 0004: steps 5 and 9 of the session lifecycle are 'the minimum durable writer check' that scope 004 names; no byte of application SQL can reach a node before step 10, and step 10 is reached only through both

Spec 0004: a permit is given back when the value that holds it is dropped, so every way out of the session task returns it, including a panic of that task; session.started is written at step 10 and each refusal adds to the counters behind session.refused

Limits table of spec 0004: handshakes (limits.handshake_max_count, the new socket is closed at once), startup deadline (limits.startup_timeout_ms), startup packet (54000), sessions (limits.session_max_count, 53300), sessions of one principal (principal[].session_max_count, 53300), backends of one node (limits.node_backend_max_count, the session waits and the probe is not counted), waiters (limits.backend_wait_max_count, 53300 at once), acquire deadline (limits.backend_acquire_timeout_ms, 53300 while waiting and 08006 while connecting), message size (54000), authentication message (1024 bytes, 08P01) and shutdown deadline; waiters are served in arrival order and there is no idle, lifetime or slow reader limit until scope 005

Memory budget of spec 0004, declared for PRD-001 AC-3: 64 MiB for the process plus 1 MiB for each session, at any setting of the limits; each direction of a session has one relay buffer of 65536 bytes (RELAY_BUFFER_BYTES), each TLS connection queues at most 65536 bytes for sending (set_buffer_limit), a startup packet, a SASL message and the kept parameter status messages are bounded, and a message body is never collected; with the default of 1000 sessions the bound is about 1 GiB

File descriptor budget of spec 0004: a session holds two, a handshake one and each node one for the probe, so the service needs an open file limit of at least twice limits.session_max_count plus limits.handshake_max_count plus 64; when an accept fails the listener counts it under session.refused with the reason accept_failed, waits 100 ms and goes on, and it never ends the daemon

Backend loss (spec 0004): when a read from or a write to the backend fails, the backend closes or it sends something that is not accepted, the session ends, POOL opens no new backend and sends nothing again (0001 SC-6); at a message boundary the client gets 08007 when a query is in flight and 08006 when none is; a query is in flight from the first byte of a Query written toward the backend until its ReadyForQuery was written to the client, so a COMMIT whose answer was lost gives 08007
When the client goes away (spec 0004): POOL closes the backend and PostgreSQL then rolls back whatever was open; POOL sends Terminate to the backend first only when no query is in flight

Shutdown (spec 0004), on SIGTERM or SIGINT: the listener stops accepting and connections still in steps 1 to 9 are closed; every session with no query in flight and the status I gets 57P01 and is ended, the others as soon as they reach that state; when limits.shutdown_timeout_ms has passed every session left is ended, with 08007 at a message boundary when a query is in flight and 57P01 when none is; then the control loop stops, the journal is closed, daemon.stopped is written and the process exits 0; drain with diagnostics is scope 008

Route view (spec 0004): the type the data plane reads, owned by pool-core and filled by the control loop in apps/pool from a TopologySnapshot: RouteView::closed(clusters) and new(routes), RouteState Open(Route) or Closed { conflict }, and Route with node, topology_epoch, authority_revision and fresh_until; a cluster the view does not hold is closed; sessions hold a watch::Receiver of it, read it in steps 5 and 9 and wake on a change while they relay; if the control loop stops publishing every route goes stale at its fresh_until

Records built in this slice (spec 0004): where each record of the Records table of spec 0003 lands: Credential, Verifier, VerifiedPrincipal, Session, Lease, LeaseGeneration and PoolKey in pool-core, ConfigurationGeneration in pool-config, TopologySnapshot and SnapshotGeneration in pool-control; the virtual cancellation credential is not built (scope 006)

Records Credential and Verifier in spec 0004 (pool-core): Debug and Display print [REDACTED], no Serialize and no Clone outside the crate; a credential is read once at start with credential generation 1 and the two SCRAM keys derived from it are kept beside it; the verifier is new in this spec, memory only, read once at start
Record VerifiedPrincipal in spec 0004 (pool-core): made only by the authentication code, holds the PrincipalId and the name, and ends with the session

Record Session in spec 0004 (pool-core): the ID is a u128 with the start sequence in the high 64 bits and a counter of this run in the low 64 bits, so it is unique across restarts without a random source; logged as 32 hex characters

Records Lease and LeaseGeneration in spec 0004 (pool-core): a lease owns the backend connection, the backend permit, the lease generation, the pool key and the private BackendKeyData, one per session and never moved (0001 SC-1); the lease generation starts at 1, is advanced for each lease, and at the largest value new sessions are refused with 53300

Record PoolKey in spec 0004 (pool-core), with the eight parts of 0001 SC-2: cluster ID, node ID, backend database, backend login, credential generation, topology epoch, TLS policy (VerifyFull) and startup profile (DedicatedV1); computed in step 6 and compared in step 9; scope 005 partitions reuse by it; Debug prints the IDs and generations and [REDACTED] for the database and the login

Log events (spec 0004): tracing is adopted for the events and the writer is first party code in apps/pool, a type that implements tracing::Subscriber, turns each event into one JSON line and ignores spans; it puts the line into a bounded queue of 1024 lines with try_send and one task writes them to stderr, so a slow reader of stderr can never hold a worker of the runtime; a full queue drops the line and counts it

Log line format of spec 0004: one JSON object with ts, level and event first, then the fields in code order; ts is UTC like 2026-11-15T08:56:01.123Z; event is a constant every call must give, and a call without it is written as log.unnamed at level error; a field value is a string, a whole number or a boolean; the level is fixed at info; nothing writes to stdout while the daemon serves

Spec 0004 log fields: the event table, with the telemetry table of spec 0003, is the permission the log rules ask for; new are the principal ID, the session ID, a SQLSTATE and counts and durations; never in any event: a principal name, a login, a database name, a host, a port, a path, SQL, a parameter value, error text from PostgreSQL, a nonce, a proof or a key (SEC-11)
Spec 0004 log event daemon.started (info; start_sequence, configuration_generation, authority_id), daemon.stopping (info; sessions) and daemon.stopped (info; no field), and log.dropped (warn; count)
Spec 0004 log event admission.changed (info; cluster_id, state open or closed, node_id when open, reasons when closed, snapshot_generation), written when the state or the reasons of a cluster change
Spec 0004 log event authority.conflict_latched (warn; cluster_id, recorded, whether the journal holds it) and journal.write_failed (error; class, the name of the JournalError)
Spec 0004 log event probe.failed (warn; node_id, class connect, tls, login, timeout or answer), written when the class of a node changes and not for every sample, and probe.recovered (info; node_id)

Spec 0004 log event session.started (info; session, principal_id, identity_id, cluster_id, node_id, lease_generation, topology_epoch) and session.ended (info; session, reason client_terminate, client_closed, backend_lost, unsupported, protocol, message_limit, conflict or shutdown; status idle, in_transaction, failed or in_flight; duration_ms)

Spec 0004 log event session.refused (warn; reason, count), one line per reason and second: handshake_limit, startup_timeout, plaintext, tls, protocol, unsupported, message_limit, authentication, unmapped, session_limit, principal_limit, closed, wait_limit, acquire_timeout, backend_unavailable, cancel_ignored, accept_failed; refusals are counted so that a flood of bad connections cannot flood the log

Spec 0004 log event backend.failed (warn; node_id, class connect, tls, auth_method, login, not_primary, protocol or timeout; sqlstate when PostgreSQL sent one; count), one line per node, class and second
